title: Bouncing ball

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with exactly known physics (restitution e = 0.72)

caveats: motion blur / stretching during fast fall

slow_motion.evidence: No on-screen text or narration indicates slow motion; motion appears as real-time animation.

subjects.description: small orange cartoon ball falling through the air

observation.what_happens: An orange ball drops from just below a black-and-white striped bar at the top and falls down and slightly to the right toward the brown ground. The free motion starts when the ball is released at the top and ends when it first contacts the ground.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself (fitted frames only): 3278 px/s² over 4 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x advances steadily while y shows repeated fall-and-rise arcs with shrinking rebound height, so motion is ballistic flight with dissipative ground bounces. g is given and fixed by the scale. Candidates share the same bounce event at a constant floor and differ only in air drag: none vs linear vs quadratic to see which extrapolates to the hidden bounces.

law.summary: The ball flies under gravity alone and bounces off the floor losing some bounce.

critique.finding: The ball drops under pull {g} to the floor at {y_floor} then bounces, keeping {e} of its upward speed.
critique.headline: Orange ball falls freely then bounces off ground
critique.why_it_won: It includes the ground bounce that the plain fall without a bounce cannot match, while added air drag changes nothing because the air effect fits to nothing.

headline: Orange ball falls freely then bounces off ground
finding: The ball drops under pull 9.81 m/s² to the floor at -1.4407 ± 0.0038 m then bounces, keeping 0.719816 ± 0.000076 of its upward speed.

eyeball.law_in_words: free fall under constant gravity with parabolic flight between impacts and vertical velocity at ground reversed and scaled by restitution e, with ball centre at contact one radius above ground
